Through that process, you will actually achieve enlightenment. The truth is it has to be personal; there can be no universal truth. You must fight for your own truth every day. Ready must thou be to burn thyself in thy own flame. Thou must destroy yourself if thou art to become new. To live is to die—thou must first destroy everything thou thinkst thou understandest in order to build a new understanding.

Though lonesome one, though go the way of the creating one; create for thyself a god out of the seven devils.

Though lonesome one, though goes the way of the loving one. Though loves thyself and despise thee as only the loving one doth despise. To create desire the loving one becomes because he despiseth. What know he of love who hath not been obliged to despise just what he loved.

When thou negate thyself, when thou move into nothingness, thou can only move into ignorance and slavery. Does that make sense? You are born of two natures; let these fight. When Zorusa had spoken these words, he paused like one who had not said his last word, and long balance the staff undouily in his hand. At least he spoke thus, and his voice had changed.

The man of knowledge must be able not only to love his enemies but also hate his friends. You want true knowledge; you can learn from me, but at the end we must leave each other and thou must say he is now thy enemy. I must now destroy him if I really want to be myself. Ye love your virtue as a mother loves her child. But when did one hear of a mother wanting to be paid for her love?

Your dearest self is thy virtue; the ring's thirst is in you to reach itself again. Struggle every ring and turn itself. And like the star that goeth out, so is every work of your virtue. Its light on its way and traveling? When will it cease to be on its way? Thus is the light of your virtue still on its way even when its work is done; be forgotten and dead, still its ray of light liveth and travelleth.

When we die, our bodies decompose; what's left is our virtue. That's who we are: all that good we've done in the world, all the knowledge, all the enlightenment, all the emotions generated. We must embrace this nature and become virtue itself. Being human is to be first and foremost virtuous, seeking Asha. For this is the truth.

I have departed from the house of scholars; I slammed the door behind me too long did my soul sit hungry at their table. Not like them have I got the knack of investigating as a knack of nutcracking. Freedom do I love in the air over fresh soil; rather would I sleep on oxkins than on their honors and indignities. I am too hot and scorched with thine own thought often ready to take away my breath. Then go, then I have to go into the open air and away from all dusty rooms.
